chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it from Al-Mufazzal, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and complained to him about conjunctivitis (eye inflammation). He said to me: 'Do you want the unique remedy?' Then he said to me: 'When you wash your hand after eating, wipe your eyebrows and say three times: Al-hamdu lillahi al-muhsini al-mujmili al-mun'imi al-mufdili (Praise be to Allah, the Bestower, the Aggregate, the Benefactor, the Gracious).' He said: 'So I did that, and my eye did not suffer from conjunctivitis after that, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds.'
ai.seo_question: What is the prophetic remedy for eye inflammation (conjunctivitis) mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes a specific spiritual and physical remedy for conjunctivitis (*al-ramad*) to the narrator al-Mufaddal, emphasizing the integration of ritual purity with divine remembrance. The practice involves wiping the eyebrows after washing hands post-meal while reciting a four-fold praise of Allah as the 'Bestower, Perfecter, and Giver of Grace,' which resulted in the narrator's eyes remaining free from the ailment. This highlights the Shia tradition of viewing prophetic and imamic teachings as holistic sources of healing, combining physical hygiene with spiritual devotion.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, raising it from Al Mufazzal who said,

‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I complained to him<sup>asws</sup> of the conjunctivitis. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Or would you like something odd?’ Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Whenever you wash your hands after the meal, so wipe your eyelids, and say three times, ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Bestower, the Aggregate, the Benefactor, the Gracious’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I did that, so I did not have conjunctivitis in my eye after that, and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the Worlds’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad in a marfu‘ manner has narrated from al-Mufaddal who has said the following: “I once visited abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and complained before him (the Imam) about eye ache. He (the Imam) said, ‘Do you want something unique?’

He (the Imam) then said to me, ‘When you wash your hands after eating food, wipe your eye brows and say three times, “All praise belongs to Allah, the Benefactor, the Graceful, the Munificent, the Pre-eminent.’” He (the narrator) has said, ‘I followed the instruction and thereafter my eyes did not experience any pain and ache, all praise belongs to Allah, Cherisher of the worlds.’”
